key_insight: A three-step, ultraviolet-free photoionization scheme rapidly loads selected barium isotopes from a naturally abundant source, with successive resonant transitions reinforcing isotope selectivity.
engineering_relevance: Rapid, high-purity loading of ¹³⁷Ba⁺ or ¹³⁵Ba⁺ could support scaling trapped-ion quantum computing and simulation systems.
method: Select neutral isotopes using the narrow 791 nm transition.
Resonantly transfer atoms at 554 nm, further suppressing unwanted isotopes.
Ionize using an existing 532 nm Raman beam.
evidence_signal: Spectral-overlap analysis supports relayed selectivity, and the authors report rapid loading with no contaminant ions detected throughout the experiment.
watch_item: The abstract gives no numerical loading rates or contamination detection limits, limiting quantitative performance assessment.
paper_title: Rapid high-purity loading of barium ion via relayed selectivity from naturally abundant source
